science.title: Forest suberin fatty acids enable tailored and layered multifunctional electrospun polycaprolactone-chitosan nanofibers
science.description: Current electrospun tissue engineering scaffolds still face challenges in simultaneously achieving adequate mechanical stability, tailored surface functionality, and multifunctional performance. To address this limitation, this study aimed to develop multifunctional biodegradable nanofibrous scaffolds using forest-derived suberin fatty acids (SFAs), selected as renewable functional additives because of their amphiphilic chemical structure and their potential to tailor both bulk and surface properties. Electrospun polycaprolactone/chitosan (PCL/CS) nanofibers were functionalized with SFA either by incorporation into the polymer matrix or by surface application through coating. The resulting nanocomposites were characterized in terms of their structural, thermal, mechanical, and biological properties by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), swelling and degradation analyses, tensile testing, antibacterial assays, and fibroblast viability studies. SEM analysis revealed that incorporating SFA into the PCL/CS matrix significantly reduced fiber diameter and narrowed the fiber diameter distribution. In contrast, coating the surface with SFA modified the fiber topography and surface compactness. Matrix incorporation of SFA enhanced early-stage water uptake and degradation, whereas surface coating resulted in a more gradual hydration response. Notably, the dual-loading system (PCL/CS/SFA + SFA coated) minimized both swelling and cumulative degradation, indicating enhanced barrier performance. Mechanical testing showed that matrix incorporation enhanced tensile strength while surface coating preserved ductility. Numerical analyses further revealed that SFA incorporation increased the critical buckling load and stress values, whereas SFA coating led to a decrease in these properties. Antibacterial assays demonstrated strong inhibition against Staphylococcus aureus (≈ 93%) with no effect on Escherichia coli. Biocompatibility studies confirmed excellent fibroblast compatibility for all SFA-modified nanofibers, while matrix incorporation of SFA favored early-stage cell proliferation. Overall, the proposed dual-functionalized PCL/CS/SFA nanofibrous system represents a sustainable strategy for tailoring both bulk and surface properties, highlighting its potential for wound dressing and other temporary biomedical applications.

science.title: Jurassic flightless bird reveals early ecological diversity of avialans
science.description: The origin and early diversification of birds remain highly debated in vertebrate evolution. Although estimates of the evolutionary timescales suggest a Jurassic period radiation1,2, a profound scarcity of fossils from this period has hampered how the distinctive bird bauplan was assembled3–5. Selection for powered flight has been viewed as the primary driver of early avialan skeletal modifications3,6,7, attesting to the independent occurrences of aerodynamic features among paravian lineages8. Here we report on the discovery of a Late Jurassic avialan, Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, gen. et sp. nov., from the Zhenghe Fauna of southeastern China9. As one of the earliest diverging avialans, Y. yangyuanensis exhibits a striking mosaic of features, combining a mixture of avialan- and troodontid-like cranial characters, paired with derived postcranial traits and a deinonychosaur-like hyperextensible second pedal digit. Phylogenetically informed analyses show that Y. yangyuanensis possesses markedly short forelimbs—a condition present widely among non-avialan theropods. These findings provide strong evidence for a terrestrial, flightless lifestyle of Y. yangyuanensis. Our study demonstrates that evolution works intensively as exemplified by the occurrence of several, divergent ecological pathways being exploited in the initial diversification of birds. A fossil bird from the Upper Jurassic Zhenghe Fauna of southeastern China contemporary with Archaeopteryx and that clearly could not fly sheds new light on the ecological diversification of early-diverging avialans.
